def.en: A set of statements in which some statements (the premises) are offered as reasons for another statement (the conclusion).
def.zh: 论证就是“用理由支持一个观点”：一句或几句是理由（前提，**premise**），另一句是这些理由要支持的观点（结论，**conclusion**）。原文里结论可能先说，也可能最后才说；写成标准形式时，前提在前，结论放在最后。哲学课里的论证不是吵架，而是一条可以一步一步检查的推理链。

example.zh: 《申辩篇》第 5 页：苏格拉底用“马只有少数养马人能养好，大多数人反而把马弄坏”等理由，支持“美勒托从没关心过年轻人”这个结论。
example.en: In the Apology (p. 5), Socrates uses the horse-breeder comparison as a reason for concluding that Meletus has never cared about the young.

def.en: A statement that an argument offers as a reason for its conclusion; in standard form the premises are numbered P1, P2, and so on.
def.zh: 前提就是论证里“当理由用”的句子。考试写标准形式（**standard form**）时，按顺序写成 P1、P2……。评价一个论证时，常常就是一条一条问：这个前提是真的吗？

example.zh: 《申辩篇》第 7 页怕死的论证里，“没有人知道死是最大的好事还是最大的坏事”就是一个前提。
example.en: In the Apology's argument about fearing death (p. 7), the claim that no one knows whether death is the greatest good or the greatest evil is a premise.

def.en: The statement that an argument tries to establish on the basis of its premises; in standard form it is written last and marked C.
def.zh: 结论是论证最终要证明的那句话；写成标准形式时放在最后，标成 C。读一篇哲学文章时，先找结论（作者到底想证明什么），再找支持它的前提。

example.zh: 《游叙弗伦篇》两难论证（第 7 页，10d）的结论是：虔敬不等于为神所爱的。
example.en: The conclusion of the dilemma argument in the Euthyphro (p. 7, 10d) is that the pious is not the same as the god-loved.

def.en: A way of setting out an argument as a numbered list of premises (P1, P2, ...) followed by the conclusion (C), so that each step can be checked.
def.zh: 把论证拆开、编号写出来：前提（**premise**）写成 P1、P2……每条一句，最后写结论 C（**conclusion**）。这样老师和你自己都能一步一步检查。本站建议：题目要你 **reconstruct**（重构）一个论证时，就把它写成标准形式。补充（读物外）：课程大纲把“从哲学文本中提取和概括论证”列为学习目标之一，标准形式是做到这一点的好办法。

example.zh: 苏格拉底驳美勒托的第二个论证可以写成：P1 坏人会伤害身边的人；P2 没人愿意受伤害；P3 苏格拉底知道，把身边的人教坏会让自己有受伤害的风险；C 所以他不会故意败坏青年：要么根本没有败坏，要么是无意的（《申辩篇》第 5 页）。
example.en: Socrates' second argument against Meletus (Apology p. 5): P1 bad people harm those close to them; P2 no one wants to be harmed; P3 Socrates knows that making his associates bad would put him at risk of harm; C so he does not corrupt the young deliberately: either he does not corrupt them at all, or he does so unwillingly.

def.en: An assumption is a claim that an argument needs in order to work but does not state openly.
def.zh: 论证没明说、却要靠它才成立的前提。评价论证时，找出隐含的假设并问“它真的对吗”，是很常见的得分点。

example.zh: 养马人类比隐含一个假设：让人变好也像养马一样，是少数专家才有的本领（《申辩篇》第 5 页）；支持民主的人可以不同意。
example.en: The horse-breeder argument assumes that making people better, like training horses, is a skill that only a few experts have (Apology p. 5).

def.en: An objection is a reason offered against a thesis or an argument, often by attacking one of its premises; a reply is the defender's answer to it.
def.zh: 反驳（**objection**）＝对一个观点或论证提出的质疑，常常是攻击其中某个前提；回应（**reply**）＝对质疑的答复。本站建议的小论文结构：论点 → 作者的论证 → 一个反驳 → 回应或你的评价。

example.zh: 《申辩篇》第 7 页：有人问他走上这条有被处死危险的路难道不羞耻（反驳）；他回答，好人做事只看对错，而且要守住自己的岗位（回应）。
example.en: In the Apology (p. 7), someone asks whether Socrates is ashamed of a life that has put him in danger of death; he replies that a good man looks only at whether he acts rightly and must hold his post.

def.en: An argument or question that allows only two options and shows that each of them leads to a difficulty or to the same conclusion; each option is called a horn of the dilemma.
def.zh: 只给两个选项，并说明选哪一个都有麻烦，或者都得出同一个结论；每个选项叫两难的一个“角”（**horn**，也可以说一“支”）。要反驳一个两难，可以说明某一个角其实走得通，或者指出还有第三个选项。

example.zh: 《游叙弗伦篇》第 7 页（10a）：神爱虔敬的东西是因为它虔敬，还是它虔敬是因为神爱它？游叙弗伦选了前一支（10d）。
example.en: Euthyphro p. 7 (10a): is the pious loved by the gods for being pious, or does their love make it pious? Euthyphro takes the first horn (10d).

def.en: An answer to the question 'What is X?' that states the one feature common to all cases of X that makes them X, so that it fits all and only the cases of X and can be used to judge new ones; a list of examples is not a definition.
def.zh: 定义回答“X 是什么”：说出所有 X 共有、并让它们成为 X 的那一个特征（型，**form**）。好的定义对所有 X 都成立，对不是 X 的东西不成立，还能拿来判断新的情况；举几个例子、列一张清单都不算定义。

example.zh: 游叙弗伦的第一个回答“虔敬就是像我现在这样起诉做错事的人”只是一个例子，不是定义（《游叙弗伦篇》第 4–5 页）。
example.en: Euthyphro's first answer, that piety is prosecuting wrongdoers as he is doing now, is an example, not a definition (Euthyphro pp. 4-5).

def.en: A reductio ad absurdum refutes a claim by showing that, together with beliefs already accepted, it leads to an absurd or contradictory result.
def.zh: 先假设对方的说法成立，再加上对方自己相信的东西，推出荒唐或自相矛盾的结论，从而证明对方的说法错了。

example.zh: “神所喜爱的就是虔敬的”，加上游叙弗伦相信的“诸神会争吵”，推出同一个行为既虔敬又不虔敬（《游叙弗伦篇》第 5–6 页）。
example.en: Defining the pious as what is dear to the gods, together with Euthyphro's belief that the gods quarrel, implies that one act is both pious and impious (Euthyphro pp. 5-6).

def.en: A craft analogy (the station's label; the readings do not use the phrase) compares a moral question with a skilled trade, such as horse breeding, medicine or shipbuilding, in which there are clear experts and clear products.
def.zh: 拿有专门技术的行业（养马、行医、造船）来比道德问题，追问：在做好人、虔敬这些最重要的事上，谁是专家？成果是什么？“技艺类比”是本站沿用的叫法，读物里没有这个词。

example.zh: 《申辩篇》第 5 页：只有少数养马人能让马变好；《游叙弗伦篇》第 9–10 页：服侍医生产生健康，服侍造船匠产生船。
example.en: Apology p. 5: only a few horse breeders make horses better; Euthyphro pp. 9-10: service to doctors produces health and service to shipbuilders produces ships.

def.en: Irony is saying something other than, or the opposite of, what one really means, as when Socrates pretends to admire someone's wisdom.
def.zh: 说的和真正的意思不一样（甚至相反），比如装谦虚、假装佩服对方。苏格拉底常用反讽请对方把自称的知识拿出来检验。

example.zh: 苏格拉底说要拜游叙弗伦为师（《游叙弗伦篇》第 3 页，5a）；《申辩篇》里他羡慕 Evenus 收费便宜（第 2 页），还说陪审员会以为他说要服从神是在反讽（第 12 页，38a）。把前两例读成反讽是本站的理解；第三例的“反讽”（ironical）是读物里苏格拉底自己用的词。
example.en: Socrates offers to become Euthyphro's pupil (Euthyphro p. 3, 5a); in the Apology he envies Evenus for teaching so cheaply (p. 2) and says the jury will think he is being ironical about obeying the god (p. 12, 38a). Reading the first two as irony is an interpretation; 'ironical' in the third is Socrates' own word.

def.en: Apologia, the Greek word behind the title Apology, means a defence speech in court, not an expression of regret.
def.zh: 希腊词 apologia 的意思是法庭上的“辩护”，英文 Apology 只是它的音译，不是“道歉”。出处是 Grube 给《申辩篇》写的导言脚注，印在《游叙弗伦篇》文件第 11 页。

example.zh: 苏格拉底不但不道歉，还拒绝乞怜，甚至提出自己应得在市政厅免费用餐（《申辩篇》第 10–11 页）。
example.en: Far from apologizing, Socrates refuses to beg for pity and even proposes free meals in the Prytaneum (Apology pp. 10-11).

terms.zh: 早先的控告者与后来的控告者

def.en: Socrates distinguishes the many nameless people who spread rumours about him for years (the old accusers) from Meletus, Anytus and Lycon, who brought the formal charge (the later accusers), and he fears the old accusers more.
def.zh: 早先的控告者：多年散布流言、大多叫不出名字的一大批人（研究天上地下、把弱论证说强、教给别人）。后来的控告者：美勒托、安尼图斯、吕孔，正式指控是败坏青年、不信城邦的神而信新的精灵之事。苏格拉底更怕早先那批：陪审员从小就听，没人反驳过，他也没法盘问他们。

example.zh: 早先的控告者里唯一能点名的是一位喜剧作家：大家在阿里斯托芬（**Aristophanes**）的喜剧里见过一个吊在半空、说自己在空中行走的苏格拉底（《申辩篇》第 2 页）。
example.en: The only old accuser who can be named is a writer of comedies: Aristophanes' play showed a Socrates swinging about and claiming to walk on air (Apology p. 2).

terms.en: Making the worse argument the stronger
terms.zh: 把较弱的论证说成较强的

def.en: This is the rumoured trick of using clever speech to make the weaker case win, which the old accusers said Socrates practised and taught to others.
def.zh: 用说话技巧让本来站不住的一方赢，也就是诡辩。这是旧流言说苏格拉底会做、还教给别人的事，后来也成了骂一切哲学家的老套话之一。

example.zh: 被苏格拉底的年轻模仿者问倒的人，说不出他到底教了什么，就搬出“研究天上地下”“不信神”“把弱论证说强”这些老套话（《申辩篇》第 4 页，23d）。
example.en: People exposed by Socrates' young imitators, unable to say what he teaches, fall back on the stock charges: studying the heavens, not believing in the gods, making the worse argument the stronger (Apology p. 4, 23d).

def.en: Well-known professional teachers of Socrates' time, such as Gorgias, Prodicus, Hippias and Protagoras, who taught young men for a fee; in the Apology Socrates denies that he teaches for fees, and in the Meno it is disputed whether the sophists really teach virtue.
def.zh: 苏格拉底那个时代有名的职业教师，收取学费教年轻人，比如高尔吉亚（**Gorgias**）、普罗狄科（**Prodicus**）、希庇亚斯（**Hippias**）和普罗泰戈拉（**Protagoras**）。《申辩篇》说前三位能到任何城邦去招学生（第 2 页），苏格拉底说自己从不收费教人；《美诺篇》里，智者是不是真能教美德有争议：安尼图斯说他们把人带坏，美诺说高尔吉亚从不承诺教美德，至于别的智者，他也拿不准。

example.zh: 卡利亚（**Callias**）在智者身上花的钱比谁都多；他说 **Evenus** 能让人成为优秀的人和公民，学费五个明那（《申辩篇》第 2 页）。
example.en: Callias, who spent more on Sophists than anyone, says that Evenus can teach human excellence for five minas (Apology p. 2).

def.en: The oracle at Delphi is the reply of the god at Delphi, given through the Pythian, to Chairephon's question whether any man was wiser than Socrates: no one was.
def.zh: 人到德尔斐问神问题，由 the Pythian 传达神的回答。凯勒丰（**Chairephon**）问有没有人比苏格拉底更有智慧，回答是没有。神谕只回答了问题，没有下命令；把检验别人当作为神服务，是苏格拉底后来的理解。补充（读物外）：the Pythian 指德尔斐神庙里替神说话的女祭司，读物里没有这样解释。

example.zh: 苏格拉底确信自己不智慧，又认为神不会说谎，于是把神谕当谜语，去找公认有智慧的人，想反驳它，结果反而证实了它（《申辩篇》第 3–4 页）。
example.en: Sure that he was not wise but that the god does not lie, Socrates treated the answer as a riddle and questioned reputedly wise men to refute it, but ended up confirming it (Apology pp. 3-4).

def.en: For Socrates, human wisdom is not thinking you know what you do not know, together with seeing that human wisdom has little or no value.
def.zh: 不以为自己知道自己不知道的事，并看清人的智慧价值很小甚至没有。苏格拉底说他只在这一小点上比别人智慧。它不等于“我知道我一无所知”：他仍然说自己知道做错事是可耻的（《申辩篇》第 7 页，29b）。

example.zh: 他和那位政治家大概都不知道真正有价值的东西，但政治家以为自己知道；苏格拉底说他自己是不知道，也不以为知道（《申辩篇》第 3 页，21d）。
example.en: Neither he nor the politician knows anything worthwhile, but the politician thinks he does, while Socrates says, 'I do not think I know what I do not know' (Apology p. 3, 21d).

def.en: Socratic examining is questioning someone who claims to know something important, to see whether his answers hold together, which usually exposes a false belief that he knows.
def.zh: 一问一答地追问自称有知识的人，看他的回答前后一不一致、站不站得住，通常会揭出对方“以为自己知道，其实不知道”。补充（读物外）：后人把这种方法叫 **elenchus**（诘问法），这个词不在译文里。

example.zh: 苏格拉底当庭盘问美勒托“谁让年轻人变好”，美勒托越答越荒唐（《申辩篇》第 5 页）；他还说死后最想做的，就是在冥界继续检验人（第 14 页）。
example.en: Socrates cross-examines Meletus about who improves the young until his answers become absurd (Apology p. 5); he even hopes to go on examining people in Hades (p. 14).

def.en: The formal charge says that Socrates believes in new spiritual things instead of the city's gods, and Meletus agrees that spirits are either gods or children of gods.
def.zh: 正式指控说苏格拉底不信城邦的神，而信新的精灵之事。苏格拉底抓住这一点：信精灵之事就得信有精灵，而精灵是神或神的孩子，所以说他“根本不信神”是自相矛盾。

example.zh: 信神的孩子却不信神，就像信有骡子却不信有马和驴一样荒唐（《申辩篇》第 6 页，27d–e）。
example.en: Believing in children of gods but not in gods would be like believing in mules but not in horses and asses (Apology p. 6, 27d-e).

def.en: False wisdom is thinking you know what you do not know, which Socrates treats as the worst kind of ignorance; fearing death is his main example.
def.zh: 以为自己有智慧、以为自己知道，其实不知道。苏格拉底说这是最该受责备的无知。“假智慧”是本站的叫法，读物的说法是：以为自己有智慧其实没有，以为自己知道其实不知道。

example.zh: 没人知道死是最大的好事还是最大的坏事，怕死的人却表现得好像知道它是最大的坏事（《申辩篇》第 7 页，29a）。
example.en: No one knows whether death is the greatest blessing or the greatest evil, yet those who fear it act as if they knew it is the greatest evil (Apology p. 7, 29a).

def.en: The soul is a person's inner self; in the Apology Socrates urges everyone to care about making the soul as good as possible, more than about the body, wealth or reputation.
def.zh: 人内在的自我。苏格拉底劝每个人关心灵魂的最好状态，胜过关心身体、钱财和名声；按本站的理解，他说的“伤害”，指的就是让一个人的灵魂变坏（读物没有直接这样定义）。

example.zh: 他问雅典人：你们只顾钱、名声和荣誉，却不关心智慧、真理和灵魂的最好状态，不觉得羞耻吗（《申辩篇》第 8 页，29d–30b）？
example.en: He asks Athenians whether they are not ashamed to care for wealth, reputation and honours but not for wisdom, truth and the best state of their souls (Apology p. 8, 29d-30b).

def.en: The excellence (Greek aretē) that makes a human being good; in the Apology Socrates urges people to care for it more than for wealth, and in the Meno the question whether it can be taught leads Socrates to ask what it is.
def.zh: 让一个人成为好人的那种优秀品质，也就是人的卓越。希腊词是 aretē：《申辩篇》31b 在 virtue 后面注了这个词（第 8 页）。《申辩篇》里苏格拉底劝人关心美德胜过关心钱财；《美诺篇》里美诺问美德能不能教，苏格拉底坚持先弄清美德到底是什么。补充（读物外）：一般认为《申辩篇》30b 的 excellence（卓越）译的也是 aretē。

example.zh: 他像父亲或兄长一样劝每个人关心美德，自己却从不收钱（《申辩篇》第 8 页，31b）；他还请陪审员将来责备他的儿子，如果他们把钱看得比美德重（第 14 页）。
example.en: Like a father or elder brother, he urged each citizen to care for virtue without ever charging a fee (Apology p. 8, 31b), and he asks the jurors to reproach his sons if they care more for money than for virtue (p. 14).

def.en: The gadfly is Socrates' image of himself as an insect that the god attached to Athens, a large but sluggish horse, to keep rousing and reproaching its citizens.
def.zh: 牛虻是叮马的飞虫。苏格拉底说雅典像一匹又大又高贵、却有点懒的马，神把他安在这座城上，整天叮醒、劝说、责备每个人；人们会烦，可杀了他，城邦就会接着睡。

example.zh: 他说自己是神送给城邦的礼物：多年不管自己的事、不收钱，贫穷就是证人（《申辩篇》第 8–9 页，30e–31c）。
example.en: He calls himself the god's gift to the city: for years he neglected his own affairs without charging fees, and his poverty is his witness (Apology pp. 8-9, 30e-31c).

def.en: Socrates' divine sign is a voice he has had since childhood that only turns him away from something he is about to do and never urges him on.
def.zh: 苏格拉底从小就有的一个声音，只阻止、从不鼓励。它阻止他从政；受审那天它一次也没出现，他由此推出发生的事可能是好的。它不是德尔斐神谕。补充（读物外）：后人常叫它 **daimonion**，这个词不在译文里。

example.zh: 征兆阻止他参与公共事务；他说一个真正为正义而战的人要想活下去，只能过私人生活（《申辩篇》第 9 页，31c–32a）。
example.en: The sign kept him out of public affairs; he says a real fighter for justice must live privately to survive (Apology p. 9, 31c-32a).

def.en: The Thirty were the harsh oligarchy that ruled Athens for about nine months in 404-3 BC, after its final defeat, and that ordered Socrates to help arrest Leon of Salamis.
def.zh: 雅典战败后建立的严苛寡头政府，公元前 404–403 年统治约九个月（《申辩篇》第 9 页脚注 4）。“三十僭主”是常见的中文叫法。

example.zh: 三十人命令苏格拉底和另外四个人去萨拉米斯抓勒翁（**Leon**）来处死；另外四人去了，苏格拉底回了家（《申辩篇》第 9 页，32c–d）。
example.en: The Thirty ordered Socrates and four others to bring Leon from Salamis to be executed; the others went, but Socrates went home (Apology p. 9, 32c-d).

def.en: A counter-assessment is the penalty that a convicted defendant proposes in reply to the prosecutor's proposal, after which the jury chooses between the two.
def.zh: 雅典的程序（Grube 的导言，《游叙弗伦篇》文件第 11 页）：定罪后，原告先提一个刑罚，被告再提一个反提刑罚，501 人的陪审团在两者中选一个。美勒托提死刑；苏格拉底先说自己应得市政厅免费用餐，最后提三十明那罚款，陪审团判了死刑。

example.zh: 苏格拉底拒绝坐牢、交不起的罚款、流放和闭嘴，先提一明那，再在柏拉图等人担保下提三十明那（《申辩篇》第 12 页，37b–38b）。
example.en: Socrates rejects prison, an unpayable fine, exile and silence, and offers one mina, then thirty minae guaranteed by Plato and others (Apology p. 12, 37b-38b).

def.en: The Prytaneum was the town hall of Athens, where victorious Olympic athletes were rewarded with free meals.
def.zh: 雅典的执政官大厅（市政厅），奥运冠军在那里享受免费用餐（《申辩篇》第 11 页脚注 5）。苏格拉底定罪后说，按应得的来算，他该得这份待遇。

example.zh: 他说冠军只让你们以为自己幸福，他让你们真的幸福；冠军不缺饭吃，他缺（《申辩篇》第 11 页，36d–e）。
example.en: He says an Olympic victor only makes people think they are happy, while he makes them happy, and the victor does not need the food but he does (Apology p. 11, 36d-e).

def.en: The unexamined life is a life without regular questioning of oneself and others about virtue and how to live; Socrates says such a life has no worth for a human being.
def.zh: 不追问、不检验自己和别人（什么是好、怎样活才对）的人生。苏格拉底说这样的人生不值得过；这句话出现在判刑阶段，是他拒绝“闭嘴过日子”的理由。

example.zh: 有人问他离开雅典后能不能安安静静、不说话过日子；他说那等于违背神，而且每天讨论美德是人最大的好事，因为“未经审视的人生不值得过”（《申辩篇》第 12 页，38a）。
example.en: Asked whether he could live quietly after leaving Athens, he says this would disobey the god, that discussing virtue every day is the greatest good for a human being, and that 'the unexamined life is not worth living for man' (Apology p. 12, 38a).

def.en: Piety (hosion) means in the first instance knowing and performing the proper rituals of prayer and sacrifice, and in its wider sense pious conduct in general, close to righteousness; the Euthyphro searches for its definition without finding one.
def.zh: 对神恰当、正确的态度和行为。Grube 说，希腊词 hosion 首先指懂得祈祷和献祭的正确仪式并照着做；游叙弗伦用的是它的宽义：一般的虔敬行为，差不多等于正义（《游叙弗伦篇》第 1 页）。苏格拉底正是以不虔敬（不敬神）的罪名被起诉的。

example.zh: 游叙弗伦说告父亲是虔敬的，他的家人说是不虔敬的；对同一件事的分歧，引出了“虔敬到底是什么”的问题（《游叙弗伦篇》第 3–4 页）。
example.en: Euthyphro calls prosecuting his father pious, while his family calls it impious, which raises the question of what piety is (Euthyphro pp. 3-4).

def.en: The king-archon was one of the nine chief magistrates of Athens, in charge of religious rites and purifications and of legal cases involving offences against the gods.
def.zh: 雅典九位主要官员之一，管宗教仪式和净化，也管冒犯神的案件（《游叙弗伦篇》第 2 页脚注 2）。苏格拉底的不敬神案和游叙弗伦的杀人案都要到他的法庭。

example.zh: 游叙弗伦在王者执政官的法庭附近碰到苏格拉底，很惊讶：苏格拉底平时在吕克昂（**Lyceum**）和年轻人谈话，不是打官司的人（《游叙弗伦篇》第 2 页）。
example.en: Meeting Socrates outside the king-archon's court surprises Euthyphro, since Socrates usually spends his time talking in the Lyceum, not in the courts (Euthyphro p. 2).

def.en: Pollution is the religious stain that Euthyphro says falls on anyone who knowingly lives with an unpunished killer, until he cleanses himself and the killer by bringing the killer to justice.
def.zh: 宗教上的不洁。游叙弗伦说，明知而和没受惩罚的杀人者同桌共食，就会沾上同样的污染，只有把他告上法庭，才能洗清他和自己（《游叙弗伦篇》第 3 页，4b–c）。

example.zh: 替游叙弗伦家干活的雇工杀了家里的一个奴隶，被父亲捆起来扔进沟里，冻饿而死；游叙弗伦以杀人罪起诉父亲，理由之一就是污染（《游叙弗伦篇》第 3 页）。
example.en: A laborer who had killed a household slave died bound in a ditch; Euthyphro prosecutes his father for murder, partly to avoid pollution (Euthyphro p. 3).

def.en: The one feature that all things of a kind share and that makes them things of that kind; a definition should state it, and once found it can serve as a model for judging whether a particular case belongs to the kind.
def.zh: 所有同类东西共有、并让它们成为这一类东西的那一个特征。定义要说出的就是它；找到了它，就能拿它当标准（范本，**model**）去判断一个具体情况算不算这一类。名称里的 eidos 是希腊词，平常指外貌（《游叙弗伦篇》译本脚注 7）。本站第 3 周的课文把 **form** 译作“型”，第 4 周的课文译作“形式”，是同一个词。注意：这两篇对话里的型还只是这个意思。脚注 7 说，早期对话里的型似乎就在具体事物之中，没有单独的存在；《美诺篇》导言（第 2 页）说，作为回忆和知识对象的柏拉图的 Forms 要到《斐多篇》（**Phaedo**）才加进来，本课程没有读这一篇。

example.zh: 苏格拉底说，他要的不是一两个虔敬行为的例子，而是让所有虔敬行为都虔敬的那个型本身，好拿它当范本去判断任何行为（《游叙弗伦篇》第 5 页，6d–e）。
example.en: Socrates does not want a couple of examples of pious actions; he wants the form itself that makes every pious action pious, so that he can use it as a model for judging any action (Euthyphro p. 5, 6d-e).

terms.zh: 为神所爱的（神所喜爱的）

def.en: The god-loved is what the gods love; Euthyphro defines the pious first as what is dear to the gods and then as what all the gods love, and both definitions fail.
def.zh: 被神喜爱的东西。“神所喜爱的就是虔敬的”被诸神意见不一驳倒；“所有神都爱的就是虔敬的”被两难驳倒：为神所爱的之所以为神所爱，是因为神爱它，而虔敬的东西是因为它虔敬才被爱。

example.zh: 最后，游叙弗伦说我们给神的只是尊敬和让神高兴的东西，虔敬又成了神所喜爱的，论证绕回原点（《游叙弗伦篇》第 10–11 页，15b–c）。
example.en: In the end Euthyphro says we give the gods only honour and what pleases them, so the pious is again what is dear to them, and the argument comes full circle (Euthyphro pp. 10-11, 15b-c).

def.en: The Euthyphro dilemma, a later name, is Socrates' question whether the gods love the pious because it is pious, or whether it is pious because the gods love it.
def.zh: 补充（读物外）：这是后人给《游叙弗伦篇》10a 这个问题起的名字，不在译文里。问题是：神爱虔敬的东西是因为它虔敬，还是它虔敬是因为神爱它？游叙弗伦选了前一支（10d），由此推出虔敬不等于为神所爱的。后人还把它推广成“对的事是因为神命令才对，还是本来就对、神才命令”。

example.zh: 苏格拉底用“被搬的、被领的、被看的”说明：被作用的东西是因为正在被作用，才成为被作用的东西；所以为神所爱的，是因为神爱它才为神所爱（《游叙弗伦篇》第 7 页，10a–c）。
example.en: Using carried, led and seen things, Socrates shows that a thing is an affected thing because it is being affected, so the god-loved is god-loved because the gods love it (Euthyphro p. 7, 10a-c).

def.en: Socrates distinguishes the nature of a thing, what it is, from a quality that merely belongs to it (an affect); for example, being loved by all the gods is only a quality of the pious, not its nature.
def.zh: 性质（遭受）＝发生在一个东西身上、它恰好具有的特点；本质＝它到底是什么。苏格拉底说，游叙弗伦只告诉了他虔敬有“被所有神爱”这个性质，没说出虔敬的本质（《游叙弗伦篇》第 8 页，11a–b）。就算所有虔敬的东西恰好都被所有神爱，“被神爱”也仍只是性质。

example.zh: 苏格拉底说：问你虔敬是什么，你没把它的本质说清楚，只告诉了我它的一种遭受或性质；它是不是被神爱，我们不争，你要从头说虔敬是什么（《游叙弗伦篇》第 8 页）。
example.en: Socrates says Euthyphro has told him 'an affect or a quality' of the pious, that it is loved by all the gods, but not what the pious is (Euthyphro p. 8, 11a).

def.en: Socrates argues that piety is a part of justice, as shame is a part of fear and odd a part of number: everything pious is just, but not everything just is pious.
def.zh: 小类在大类里面，但大类里不都是小类。Grube 说这一段（11e–12d）讲清了属（**genus**，大类）与种（**species**，小类）的区别（《游叙弗伦篇》第 1 页）。要定义一个部分，还得说清是哪一部分，比如偶数是能分成两个相等部分的那部分数。

example.zh: 很多人怕生病、怕穷，却不觉得羞耻；但感到羞耻的人总怕坏名声。所以羞耻是恐惧的一部分，就像奇数是数的一部分（《游叙弗伦篇》第 8 页，12b–c）。
example.en: Many people fear disease and poverty without feeling shame, but anyone who feels shame fears a bad reputation, so shame is a part of fear, as odd is a part of number (Euthyphro p. 8, 12b-c).

def.en: Euthyphro's fourth answer makes piety the part of justice that is care of the gods; Socrates rejects it because care benefits and improves its object, and no pious act makes a god better.
def.zh: 游叙弗伦的第四个回答（本站叫 D4）：虔敬是正义中照料神的那一部分，照料人的是正义的其余部分。照料让被照料者得到好处、变得更好（养马人照料马、猎人照料狗、养牛就是照料牛）；可虔敬的事不会让神变好，所以不是这种照料。

example.zh: 苏格拉底问：你做一件虔敬的事，就让某个神变好了？游叙弗伦说：凭宙斯发誓，不是（《游叙弗伦篇》第 9 页，13c）。
example.en: Asked whether doing something pious makes one of the gods better, Euthyphro swears by Zeus that it does not (Euthyphro p. 9, 13c).

def.en: Euthyphro then says piety is the kind of care slaves give their masters, a service to the gods; Socrates asks what main product the gods achieve through this service, and Euthyphro cannot say.
def.zh: 游叙弗伦修正说：是奴隶照料主人那种照料，也就是服侍。服侍的重点是帮主人完成目标，每种服侍都有主要产物；游叙弗伦只说神做成很多好东西，说不出主要产物，这个定义就没说完。

example.zh: 服侍医生是为了健康，服侍造船匠是为了造出船；将军的主要成果是胜利，农夫的是粮食（《游叙弗伦篇》第 9–10 页，13d–14a）。
example.en: Service to doctors aims at health and service to shipbuilders at a ship; the main achievement of generals is victory, and of farmers food (Euthyphro pp. 9-10, 13d-14a).

def.en: When piety is defined as knowing how to sacrifice and pray, Socrates shows that it becomes a skill of giving to and asking from the gods, a kind of trade from which the gods gain nothing.
def.zh: 游叙弗伦最后一个回答（本站叫 D5）：虔敬就是懂得怎样献祭和祈祷。苏格拉底推出：献祭＝给神东西，祈祷＝向神要东西，虔敬就成了神和人之间的交易技艺。可神从我们这里得不到好处，只得到尊敬和让神高兴的东西，于是又绕回“神所喜爱的”。

example.zh: 苏格拉底说，这样虔敬就成了神和人之间的一种交易技艺；游叙弗伦说：你愿意这么叫就这么叫吧（《游叙弗伦篇》第 10 页，14e）。
example.en: Socrates calls it 'a sort of trading skill between gods and men' (Euthyphro p. 10, 14e), and Euthyphro accepts the name only if Socrates prefers it.

def.en: Aporia, a later name, is the state of puzzlement in which a Socratic dialogue such as the Euthyphro ends, when no proposed definition survives examination.
def.zh: 补充（读物外）：这是后人给苏格拉底式对话这种结尾起的名字，不在译文里：所有定义都被驳倒，谁也走不下去。Grube 只说，和往常一样，没有找到让苏格拉底满意的定义（《游叙弗伦篇》第 1 页）。没找到答案不等于虔敬不存在。

example.zh: 论证绕回原点，苏格拉底要从头再来，像不放走普罗透斯（**Proteus**）那样不放游叙弗伦走；游叙弗伦却说赶时间，走了（《游叙弗伦篇》第 11 页，15c–16a）。
example.en: When the argument comes full circle, Socrates wants to start again and will not let Euthyphro go, as one must hold on to Proteus; Euthyphro says he is in a hurry and leaves (Euthyphro p. 11, 15c-16a).
